description: F-CORE-047 in the shipped German pack: a capital company has no private account. THE RULE. A GmbH's assets are separate from its shareholders' (§ 13 Abs. 1 GmbHG, § 1 Abs. 1 AktG), so what a shareholder takes out is always one of four things — salary, a loan, an open distribution, or, if it is none of those, a hidden one (§ 8 Abs. 3 Satz 2 KStG). None of the four is a private withdrawal, so a posting to 2400 Privat does two kinds of damage: it mixes the company's assets with the shareholder's, and it hides WHICH of the four actually happened, which is precisely the question a tax audit asks. WHY THE RULE HANGS ON THE LEGAL FORM AND NOT ON THE ACCOUNT, which is the whole reason this module exists: 2400 is exactly the right account for a sole trader, a GbR, an OHG and a KG, and the SAME chart serves both worlds, because German charts of accounts are not split by legal form. A prohibition attached to the account would therefore be either wrong for the partnerships or inert for the corporations. WHY IT IS A USAGE RULE AND NOT A COMBINATION: the statement is `this tenant may not post to this account`, not `these two accounts may not meet`. The old vocabulary could have faked it with `whenAccountIn: 2400–2400` plus `forbidAccountIn: 0000–9999` — every entry has at least two accounts, so it would fire — and that trick is wrong twice: it reads as a range, and account numbers compare by CODE POINT, so `0000`–`9999` does not cover a chart whose numbers start with a letter and covers a six-digit chart only by accident. THE DORMANT CASE IS PINNED FIRST, and deliberately: a tenant that never declared a legal form has none, and a rule conditioned on a fact that is absent does not apply. Refusing the posting would punish a tenant for not having configured something; applying the rule anyway would assume a precondition nobody checked.

input.text: Entnahme, bevor eine Rechtsform erklaert ist

expect.comment: DORMANT. No legal form has been declared, so the condition cannot be evaluated and the rule does not apply. `tenantConfiguration` still reports the rule, which is how a caller tells `there is no such rule` from `the rule is waiting for a fact`.
The identical posting, refused because one configuration call happened in between. Nothing about the entry changed — the tenant did.

A usage rule names one account and refuses nothing else. Worth pinning, because a rule that forbids an account by forbidding it to meet ANY other account — the trick this word replaced — is one edit away from refusing the whole chart.

THE OTHER HALF, and the reason the condition exists at all: for a sole trader 2400 is the correct account and the same chart offers it. A prohibition attached to the account instead of the legal form would have made the German pack unusable for every partnership in it.

Two private withdrawals stand, one from before the legal form was declared and one from after it was changed to a sole trader; the GmbH's attempt is not in the books at all. The bank carries all three movements that succeeded.
